Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just go by my first name for this, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was driving on a multi-lane road in League City, Texas, heading toward the freeway. Traffic was moderate, and it
was still daylight.
Q: What were you doing right before the impact?
A: I was changing lanes to get over to the right because my exit was coming up. I checked my mirror, saw what I
thought was a clear space, and started to move over.
Q: Did you use your turn signal?
A: Yes, I put my signal on a few seconds before I started moving.
Q: What happened next?
A: The other vehicle was in the lane I was moving into. It came up alongside me and we sideswiped each other. I
heard a loud scrape, and my car jerked a little toward the curb before I got it under control.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before contact?
A: Not really. It seemed to come out of my blind spot quickly, which is why I didn't catch it.
Q: How are you feeling physically since the collision?
A: My neck is sore and stiff. I've had a headache too, and turning my head to look over my shoulder hurts. I've been
using a cold pack and taking over-the-counter pain relievers.
Q: Have you sought medical attention?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same afternoon. They diagnosed a neck strain and told me to rest and follow up
with my regular doctor if it doesn't improve.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get my car fixed and feel normal again.
Q: Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the statement.
</page>
